title: NASA and SpaceX schedule 35th commercial resupply mission for October 13
excerpt: The Dragon spacecraft will carry over 6,300 pounds of science experiments and supplies to the International Space Station.
bodyHtml:
NASA and SpaceX are targeting 6:33 a.m. EDT, Oct. 13, for the launch of the 35th commercial resupply services mission to the International Space Station. The mission will utilize a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft launched on a Falcon 9 rocket from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.

The spacecraft is scheduled to dock autonomously around 11 a.m. on Oct. 15 to the space-facing port of the station’s Harmony module. The cargo includes the final set of International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Arrays, hardware to manufacture artificial retinas in microgravity, and 3D heart tissues models to advance large-scale drug testing.

The spacecraft will also carry materials to study how a new type of glass forms in microgravity and brain organoids that could reveal treatment targets for neurodegenerative diseases. The Dragon spacecraft is scheduled to remain at the space station until mid-November when it will depart the orbiting laboratory and return to Earth with time-critical research and cargo, splashing down off the coast of California.
